design: EventOperationsCoordinator composes the sealed CanonicalEventBackbone exclusively through its public publish()/consume() methods; publish_with_backpressure() enforces a bounded per-tenant in-flight admission quota before ever touching the real backbone; a BackboneError from publish() is recorded as an immutable DeadLetter, classified PERMANENT until the same event_id has failed POISON_THRESHOLD=3 times, at which point it is quarantined behind an explicit release_for_operator_replay() operator gate; replay() always reconstructs the envelope via CanonicalIngestionEnvelope.from_mapping() and re-calls the real backbone's publish(), so an incompatible schema or a lost/missing marking is blocked on replay exactly as it would be on a fresh publish -- never bypassed -- and an already-durable idempotency key is a safe no-op via the backbone's own idempotency handling, never a duplicate canonical effect

requirement_results.command: a valid event publishes through the bounded per-tenant admission quota and is delivered by the real backbone with no dead letter recorded
a tenant already at its bounded in-flight quota is refused admission (BACKPRESSURE_EXCEEDED) before ever touching the real backbone
a real publish failure (unknown schema) against the live backbone is recorded as an immutable PERMANENT dead letter with the real failure's own reason_code
the same event failing 3 times against the real backbone is classified POISON and quarantined
a POISON-classified dead letter cannot be replayed without an explicit, separate operator release (OPERATOR_GATE_CLOSED)
operator release of a POISON event does not bypass the real backbone's own schema compatibility check on replay (UNKNOWN_SCHEMA)
a replay whose reconstructed envelope has lost its classification marking is blocked exactly like a fresh publish would be (MISSING_CONTEXT), never bypassed
replaying a dead letter for an already-durable idempotency key preserves the original event_id and never creates a second real record on the live topic
full local pytest regression with a real live PostgreSQL DSN set, no new failures versus the pre-existing sandbox baseline (the two known interpreter-pin failures are unrelated and pre-existing)
